risks.note: Any decline in QAAUM, whether from market depreciation, investor redemptions or other factors, directly reduces management fee income, which is the Company's core revenue engine.
risks.risk: Revenues and profitability are directly linked to QAAUM (Internal Risk Factor 1)

risks.note: A significant portion of operating expenses - employee costs, technology infrastructure, regulatory compliance and distribution support - is relatively fixed in the short to medium term, so any material decline in QAAUM-linked revenues could disproportionately hit profitability.
risks.risk: Fixed cost base creates disproportionate profit sensitivity to a QAAUM decline

risks.note: Management fees vary significantly by category; equity-oriented and actively managed schemes earn higher fee rates than debt-oriented and passive funds. A mix shift to passives or debt, driven by investor preference, market conditions or regulation, would cut weighted average fee realisation and reduce revenue and profitability even with no fall in absolute QAAUM. This is structurally live given passives are already ₹4,055.26 billion (13.76% of total QAAUM) and the Company is the largest passive manager in India.
risks.risk: Adverse shift in QAAUM composition toward lower-fee products

risks.note: Investor redemptions in response to poor scheme performance, market volatility or changing investor preferences could cause a significant QAAUM decline; the RHP singles out large-scale redemptions by institutional investors or high-net-worth individuals.
risks.risk: Large-scale redemption risk, particularly from institutional investors and HNIs

business_ops.seasonality: Stated verbatim in the DRHP: 'Our business is not subject to seasonal variations.' The DRHP further states that there are no separate reportable segments - the Company is in the business of providing asset management services to SBI Mutual Fund and portfolio management and advisory services to clients, its financial statements are largely reflective of the asset management business, and all assets of the Group are domiciled in India. Revenue is instead driven by market levels: management fees constituted 96.47% of revenue from operations for Fiscal 2026 and are calculated as a percentage of AUM, so QAAUM movements from market depreciation, redemptions or product-mix shifts flow directly into revenue. The DRHP notes increased volatility in global and Indian capital markets since March 31, 2026 and that financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 had not been prepared as of the date of the document.
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Not a manufacturing issuer - there is no physical supply chain. The equivalent vertical structure is distribution and parentage. The Company is the investment manager to SBI Mutual Fund (India's oldest AMC lineage; SBI Mutual Fund commenced operations in June 1987 as the first mutual fund entity outside the Unit Trust of India) and operates a pan-India omnichannel distribution model integrating physical and digital platforms. Third-party distribution as at March 31, 2026 comprised 132,519 institutional and individual mutual fund distributors (MFDs), including 122,460 independent financial advisors (IFAs), 9,964 national distributors (NDs) and 95 banks (including SBI); the DRHP does not print a direct-versus-distributor or channel-wise percentage split of AUM or revenue. Digital distribution runs through integration of mutual fund investment capabilities into SBI's YONO digital banking platform (100+ million YONO users as at March 31, 2026) and the proprietary InvesTap mobile application, which had 3.97 million registered users, 3.39 million active users, a 57.17% activation rate and 5.8 million downloads as at March 31, 2026; specialized B2B applications 'Partner' and 'Mitra' support the distributor network. Dual promoter parentage is presented as the structural distribution advantage: State Bank of India (established 1806; total assets of ₹ 83,215.7 billion, 23,265 branches and over 530 million customers as of March 31, 2026, and 246 international touch points across 29 countries) and Amundi (Amundi India Holding, a wholly owned subsidiary of Amundi Asset Management; Amundi group has close to €2.4 trillion of assets under management, more than 200 million retail clients, 5,400 employees across 34 countries including 905 investment professionals, and 1,000 institutional and corporate clients as at March 31, 2026, with approximately €543.00 billion in ETF AUM), providing access to Amundi's global distribution network across Europe, the Middle East and Asia. Scale economics are stated as operating expenses of 0.08% of QAAUM for Fiscal 2026, described as the lowest among the top 10 AMCs in India, against a range of 0.10% to 0.25% for the remaining top 10 AMCs in the same period (Source: CRISIL Report). Stated operating margin (revenue from operations less operating expenses, divided by total QAAUM of mutual fund and AIF) was 0.27% (FY26), 0.25% (FY25) and 0.21% (FY24); excluding passives it was 0.37% (FY26), 0.35% (FY25) and 0.30% (FY24). Ownership history: incorporated in 1992, received SEBI approval to act as asset manager to SBI Mutual Fund in 1993, became a joint venture in 2004 when Societe Generale Asset Management S.A. acquired a 37% stake, with Amundi India Holding succeeding to that shareholding following the 2011 merger of Credit Agricole's and Societe Generale's asset management businesses.

financial_valuation.detail: Management fee income is a percentage of scheme AUM, so mark-to-market depreciation, higher net redemptions or slower fresh inflows reduce revenue proportionately. Market downturns compound NAV depreciation with behavioural redemption and SIP discontinuance. Redemptions can force selling at unfavourable prices, deepening NAV decline and triggering further redemptions across the scheme range. Debt and debt-hybrid schemes face acute liquidity risk in stressed markets and from credit events.

strategy_growth.detail: The Indian asset management industry is highly competitive across large domestic AMCs, bank-sponsored AMCs, foreign managers, specialised boutiques, PMS/AIF platforms and other financial services providers. Emerging pressure comes from direct indexing and separately managed account platforms bypassing pooled vehicles, the structural shift to direct plans, DIY investors and robo-advisers, and new entrants. Competition also extends to distribution access, investment talent and alternative products such as bank fixed deposits, direct equity, PMS, ULIPs, government savings schemes and real estate.

strategy_growth.title: RF 16 - Competition from other asset management companies and alternative investment products

concerns_observed: The Offer is 100% an Offer for Sale of up to 203,709,239 Equity Shares by State Bank of India (128,334,397) and Amundi India Holding (75,374,842). The Company receives no proceeds, so there is no fresh issue, no object-wise deployment schedule, no project cost and no monitoring agency - the only stated non-monetary object is the benefit of listing.

Net worth fell from Rs 82,975.33 mn (FY25) to Rs 59,630.62 mn (FY26) after an interim dividend of Rs 55,155.16 mn charged to retained earnings (dividend paid in cash flows Rs 55,151.32 mn), of which the related-party table shows Rs 34,146.00 mn paid to State Bank of India and Rs 20,054.00 mn to Amundi India Holding. RoNW rising from 33.77% to 43.02% is therefore driven by a shrunken equity base, not by an operating step-up; NAV per Equity Share stands at Rs 29.28 and financing cash flow was Rs -54,577.94 mn.

Fee mix is structurally adverse: passives are 32.42% of mutual fund QAAUM but generate only 5.37% of management fee income, while active equity/equity-hybrid at 42.53% of QAAUM generates 75.29%. The SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026 (notified January 14, 2026, effective April 1, 2026) lower BER caps by 10-15 bps across most categories and discontinue the 5 bps exit-load allowance, against a weighted average TER of 0.88% (FY26).

Revenue is single-line and concentrated: management fees were 96.47% of revenue from operations (FY26); top 5 schemes were 42.57% of mutual fund QAAUM and the single largest scheme 16.85%; top 5 distributors were 25.26% of MAAUM; and the investment management agreement with the Trustee Company is terminable on not less than 180 days' notice, which the RHP says would 'effectively terminate our business as an asset management company'.

Relative scheme performance deteriorated in the offer year: bottom-quartile equity and equity-oriented schemes rose to 9 (33.33% of equity schemes) at March 31, 2026 from 4 (15.38%) at March 31, 2025, and the share of industry SIP inflows fell from 12.9% (FY24) to 12.5% (FY25) to 11.4% (FY26).

Governance churn at the top: Debasish Mishra is the third MD & CEO in roughly 20 months (Shamsher Singh to November 22, 2024; Nand Kishore from November 23, 2024 with no cessation date stated anywhere in the document); his appointment effective July 1, 2026 was still 'subject to approval of the Shareholders in the ensuing AGM scheduled on July 17, 2026' - nine days after the RHP date of July 8, 2026 - and his stated term is only two years.

A 3:1 bonus of 1,526,495,460 Equity Shares on December 19, 2025 quadrupled the share count from 508,831,820 to 2,035,327,280 weeks before filing at nil acquisition price, and auditor-certified promoter weighted average cost of acquisition is Rs 0.15 (State Bank of India) and Rs 4.35 (Amundi India Holding) against an Offer Price printed as a placeholder.

The Alternates engine leans on one institutional relationship: the Company has received a reallocation notice under its fixed income mandate from a statutory provident fund institution (it held a 49.9% share of that institution's equity corpus at March 31, 2026), and states the current impact is marginal but that further non-retention 'could lead to a significant decline in assets under management'.

Regulatory friction is running, not historical: SEBI inspections for Fiscals 2023-2025 produced 16 mutual fund/RTA observations plus 6 PMS observations including administrative warnings, a voluntary settlement application proposing Rs 0.30 mn is pending before SEBI for the SBI Investment Opportunities Fund (IFSC) FPI breach, and the Fiscal 2026 SEBI inspection had not yet been initiated as at the RHP date.

Quantified legal and tax exposure with no provision: proceedings against the Company aggregate Rs 1,485.53 million and 'our Company has not made any provision for pending legal proceedings involving our Company'; contingent liabilities are Rs 1,762.09 million (2.96% of net worth), dominated by a Rs 1,319.30 million GST tax-and-penalty demand for July 2017 - October 2018 confirmed by the Commissioner (Appeals) on February 12, 2026 and now on appeal before the GST Appellate Tribunal.

The brand is licensed, not owned: the SBI logo is unregistered and used under a licence terminable at SBI's notice or if SBI Group shareholding falls below 26% on a fully diluted basis; logo royalty was Rs 506.32 mn in FY26 (5.22% of total expenses) versus Rs 266.24 mn in FY24.

Free float is thin and control is entrenched: promoters hold 98.19% of paid-up capital (97.99% fully diluted) with only 24,081 public shareholders holding 1.81%, no public holder reaching 1%, and an Inter-se Agreement dated March 19, 2026 between State Bank of India and Amundi India Holding governing board appointments, articles amendments, new business, asset sales and share issuances - an agreement to which the Company is not a party.
data_gaps: PAT margin, RoE and RoCE are null for all three fiscals. This is a routing gap in our own extraction pipeline - the 'Basis for Offer Price' KPI section was not routed into the financials bundle - not an issuer disclosure failure; the RHP does print RoNW (43.02% / 33.77% / 36.05%) and EBITDA margin (92.46% / 94.86% / 101.05%), which were captured.

No valuation multiple can be stated: the price band, Offer Price, Offer size, estimated Offer expenses, the issuer's P/E, the post-Offer capital and the post-Offer promoter shareholding are all printed as placeholders in the RHP.

Litigation totals are deliberately left null. The RHP prints no grand total, each row is qualified 'to the extent quantifiable' and includes amounts claimed jointly and severally, matters filed BY the parties (Rs 741,011.91 mn, overwhelmingly SBI's own recovery litigation as a bank) are opposite in direction to matters filed AGAINST them, director-capacity matters are folded into the SBI promoter rows, and the criminal count against the promoters is unquantified ('See note 4'). The only figure attributable to the issuer is Rs 1,485.53 mn against the Company.
The content of the CARO 2020 observations for FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024 sits in Note 54, which is not in the routed extract.
Total debt is not printed in the restated balance sheet extract, so leverage cannot be assessed; working capital days are not applicable to an asset manager and are null.

Board committee constitutions (Audit, NRC, Stakeholders' Relationship, Risk Management), the Key Managerial Personnel and Senior Management section, directors' shareholding and remuneration terms are absent - the 'Our Management' extract ends at the director biographies, which are themselves truncated mid-sentence so Sanjay Prakash's qualification and experience are unavailable.

Related-party quantum is complete only for FY2025-26; the FY2024-25 table is truncated mid-row and the FY2023-24 table is absent. Amounts are disclosed by relationship category, so single counterparties inside 'Fellow subsidiaries', 'Enterprises under common control' and 'Other related parties' cannot be named.

The 'Government and Other Approvals' extract is truncated, so the RHP's own lists of approvals applied-for-but-not-received, expired, or required-but-not-obtained are not available; their absence here is a coverage gap, not evidence that none exist.

The derived panel's contingent-liability field pct_of_networth reads 29.55, which is inconsistent with the RHP's own printed 2.96% of net worth (Rs 1,762.09 mn against net worth of Rs 59,630.62 mn); the RHP-printed 2.96% is used throughout this verdict.

Prior-year NAV per Equity Share is not carried in the extraction - only the FY26 figure of Rs 29.28 - so the fall in book value per share is described through net worth (Rs 82,975.33 mn to Rs 59,630.62 mn) rather than a per-share comparison.

The internal peer set returned by our matcher (NUVAMA, GCSL, SHAREINDIA) is not comparable to an AMC; the RHP's own five-name listed peer table (ICICI Prudential AMC, HDFC AMC, Nippon Life India AMC, Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC, UTI AMC) is the only usable comparison, and face values differ across it (Rs 1 / Rs 5 / Rs 10) so per-share figures are not directly comparable.
All 79 numbered risk factors in the document were captured (RF 1-52 internal, 53-61 external, 62-79 offer-related), so risk coverage is complete even where individual sections above are not.

verdict.our_read: India's largest AMC by mutual fund QAAUM (Rs 12,509.98 bn, 15.3% share; FY26 revenue Rs 43,894.88 mn at 92.46% EBITDA margin) sold entirely as a secondary at an unprinted price, whose thesis rides on AUM-linked fees surviving the April-2026 BER cap cuts.

red_flags: Pre-IPO capital extraction: an interim dividend of Rs 55,155.16 mn in FY26 cut net worth from Rs 82,975.33 mn to Rs 59,630.62 mn, with Rs 34,146.00 mn to State Bank of India and Rs 20,054.00 mn to Amundi India Holding - the same two parties selling in the Offer - and the resulting smaller equity base is what lifts RoNW to 43.02% from 33.77%.

The MD & CEO disclosed on the Board with effect from July 1, 2026 had not been approved by shareholders as at the RHP date; approval was scheduled for an AGM on July 17, 2026, nine days after the July 8, 2026 RHP.

3:1 bonus issue on December 19, 2025 (1,526,495,460 shares to 15,533 allottees at nil cost) quadrupling the share count weeks before the filing, flagged in the document's own bonus-within-18-months test.
Rs 85.69 mn loan written off to the SBI Funds Management Limited Employee Welfare Trust - a controlled trust - in the year immediately preceding the Offer.

CARO 2020 observations exist for all three restated fiscals (FY2026, FY2025, FY2024) per the examination report of Kirtane & Pandit LLP; their content sits in Note 54 and is not reproduced in the routed extract, so it cannot be assessed.

Auditor changed in the year immediately preceding the Offer at two group entities: SBI Funds Management (International) Private Limited (Grant Thornton to Chartist Associates LLP for FY2026) and SBI Pension Funds Private Limited (Desai, Saksena & Associates to Shah & Modi for FY2026).

Historical corporate records are untraceable - Form 2 for the June 30, 1992 further issue and the offer and allotment letters for the November 7, 1997 rights issue (independent company secretary report dated March 2, 2026; RoC intimated) - and the Company is still awaiting its authorised dealer bank's response on Form FC-GPR for certain non-resident holders in the December 2025 bonus issue.

Rs 1,319.30 mn GST demand (Rs 659.65 mn tax plus an equal penalty) on input tax credit for July 2017 - October 2018, confirmed against the Company by the Commissioner (Appeals) on February 12, 2026 and carried as a contingent liability with no provision made.

Conflicts are structural: schemes held securities issued by SBI and its associates of Rs 344.31 billion at March 31, 2026; a director of the Issuer also sits on the two-member board of the promoter Amundi India Holding; and BRLM SBI Capital Markets is an associate of both the Company and SBI, restricted to marketing the Offer.

Promoter-level regulatory history disclosed in the RHP: AMF Enforcement Committee fines of Rs 2,200.50 mn on Amundi Asset Management and Rs 616.14 mn on Amundi Intermediation (orders dated August 4, 2021, paid), and pending Yes Bank matters (SEBI Rs 250.00 mn penalty stayed by SAT; NSE Clearing matter on appeal to the Supreme Court).
strengths_observed: Largest asset management company in India by mutual fund QAAUM - Rs 12,509.98 billion and 15.3% market share as at March 31, 2026, a position held since March 2021, on total QAAUM of Rs 29,461.05 billion (Source: CRISIL Report, commissioned and paid for by the Company).

Earnings scale and trajectory: revenue from operations Rs 26,905.58 mn (FY24) to Rs 35,977.57 mn (FY25) to Rs 43,894.88 mn (FY26); PAT Rs 20,727.85 / 25,401.54 / 30,673.76 mn; basic EPS Rs 10.29 / 12.53 / 15.08 (all restated for the 3:1 bonus per Ind AS 33).

Lowest operating expense ratio among the top 10 AMCs in India at 0.08% of QAAUM for Fiscal 2026 versus a 0.10%-0.25% range for the remaining top 10 (Source: CRISIL Report, page 222); stated operating margin on mutual fund and AIF QAAUM improved 0.21% (FY24) to 0.25% (FY25) to 0.27% (FY26).

Sticky systematic book: 16.21 million live SIPs as at March 31, 2026 of which 15.87 million have been active for 37 months or more; SIP AUM Rs 1,729.17 billion; monthly SIP inflow Rs 24.79 bn (FY24) to Rs 40.59 bn (FY26).

Distribution reach that is hard to replicate: 132,519 MFDs (122,460 IFAs, 9,964 NDs, 95 banks including SBI), SBI's YONO platform with 100+ million users, InvesTap with 3.97 million registered users, and 94.25% of Fiscal 2026 transactions by volume executed digitally.

Alternates provide a second, non-mutual-fund revenue pool: PMS and advisory QAAUM Rs 16,878.99 billion (57.29% of total QAAUM) with a 39.7% share of the PMS segment, plus AIF QAAUM Rs 65.65 billion (29.18% CAGR FY24-FY26).
Passive leadership as the industry mixes toward index products: ETF and index fund QAAUM Rs 4,055.26 billion and a 27.9% share of the passive segment as at March 31, 2026, held since March 2021.

Deepest B-30 franchise among the top 10 AMCs: B-30 MAAUM Rs 2,772.77 billion = 22.82% of mutual fund MAAUM versus an industry average of 18.2%, with presence in 98.19% of India's pin codes and 19.2% share of industry B-30 MAAUM.
Operating cash generation improved every year: CFO Rs 14,382.06 mn (FY24) to Rs 19,923.76 mn (FY25) to Rs 24,876.04 mn (FY26); nil exceptional items in all three restated fiscals.

Investment platform depth: 71 investment professionals with average 9 years at the Company and 17.8 years total experience, research coverage of over 450 companies (over 85% of the BSE 500 by market capitalisation) and over 250 fixed income issuers; investment-team attrition 10.29% (FY26).
